Invited Speakers

All speakers listed below are confirmed.

Together they represent substantial institutional and geographic diversity, with a balanced mix of junior and senior researchers.

BA
Bo An

Nanyang Technological University

President's Chair Professor and Senior Faculty

“Multi-Agent Preference Modeling and Strategic Alignment”

A senior leader in artificial intelligence and multi-agent systems. His expertise brings a multi-agent and strategic perspective to preference modeling and alignment under interaction.

MA
Maksym Andriushchenko

Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems

Principal Investigator

“Failure Modes and Evaluation Gaps in Post-Training Pipelines”

Leads a group focusing on LLMs. His work offers a practitioner-informed perspective on failure modes, misspecification, and evaluation gaps in post-training pipelines.

DF
Dylan Foster

Microsoft Research

Principal Researcher

“Statistical–Computational Trade-offs in Interactive LLM Training”

A leading theorist in interactive decision-making. His contributions directly inform computational–statistical trade-offs and identifiability in modern LLM training.

WS
Weijie Su

University of Pennsylvania

Associate Professor of Statistics and Data Science

“Rigorous Statistical Foundations for RLHF and Post-Training”

A leading statistician whose recent work develops rigorous statistical foundations for LLMs. His research directly addresses identifiability, misspecification, and validity questions in RLHF and related methods.

WS
Wen Sun

Cornell University & Databricks AI

Assistant Professor

“Coverage, Exploration, and Robustness in Post-Training”

A leading researcher in reinforcement learning theory and RLHF. His work bridges theory and practice, offering formal insights into coverage, exploration, and robustness in post-training pipelines.
